habitat: Singly, and sometimes in groups when feeding, at almost any freshwater locality and at estuaries. It feeds in the shallows, shuffling its feet, and may hover before swooping. The huge domed nest is in a waterside tree or on a cliff.
summary: A common resident. A small dull-brown waterbird with a large backward-projecting crest and a heavy conical black bill. The legs are black. The sexes are alike and the immature is similar. In flight it may give a nasal wek, and at rest a wavering wek-wek-warrrrk. The page heading uses the family name Scopidae; this list keeps Scopus umbretta. The Kemp name Hamerkop and the code RB were left unchanged.

calls.description: In flight it sometimes utters a nasal 'wek… wek… wek…'. At rest it may repeat a wavering, high-pitched 'wek-wek-warrrrk'. The grade A call is from Kruger, near Skukuza. The filename is XC983782-20250327_060917_KNP_CCS_HamerKop_soundLibrary.mp3.
